newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels may resume offensive after Mobutu snub.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels may resume offensive after Mobutu snub.

text.p: Zaire rebels looked set to resume their whirlwind offensive after President Mobutu Sese Seko defiantly rejected their deadline for him to quit and said he had no plans to go into exile.
Rebel radio reminded Mobutu, Zaire's ruler since 1965 and now ailing with cancer, on Saturday that time was running out.
"Mr Mobutu has just 24 hours thanks to the extreme generosity of the alliance. He has only two choices -- to resign or to go into exile," it said.

But Mobutu, 66, looking in better health than on recent appearances, said: "This kind of joke will backfire...I am head of state. My country is Zaire and I don't know of anyone who has proposed my exile."
The rebels, who have met little resistance from Mobutu's rapidly retreating army, were consolidating their positions ahead of the expiry of the deadline.

In the second city of Lubumbashi, hundreds of former government soldiers lined up to join rebel ranks. Some 400 men of the 21st Leopard infantry brigade switched sides three days ago to help rebels to capture the city.

Rebel leader Laurent Kabila declared from Thursday a three-day "pause" in the advance of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo/Zaire (AFDL) after overrunning Lubumbashi, capital of the mineral-rich Shaba region.
The rebels, who took up arms in October, control half of the sprawling and potentially rich Central African nation, including its economic heartland with its diamond, copper, cobalt and gold mines.
Mobutu, appearing with his new emergency rule prime minister, did not rule out direct talks with Kabila, although he said the rebel leader should ask him politely.

"If he asks me politely I cannot refuse to talk to a compatriot but (for him) to be in Goma (rebel headquarters in east Zaire) and say I give him three days, it's not my style or nature. I cannot reply," Mobutu told reporters.

Rejecting calls from his one-time Western allies to stand down, he said: "I am not a colony of the Westerners...It's because of copper, cobalt, gold and diamonds that they are in the process of arming Kabila. It's not because they like Zaire."
Mobutu, who had prostate cancer surgery in Europe last August, said his opponents had taken advantage of his illness to try to topple him.
"All that has happened was because I was ill. I was on my sick bed when the affair started so I was stabbed in the back," he said.
He dismissed suggestions that the rebels were 300 km (200 miles) from the capital Kinshasa.

Mobutu declared a national state of emergency on Tuesday and named General Likulia Bolongo as prime minister, shunting aside his veteran opposition foe Etienne Tshisekedi, who had held the job less than a week.

He was speaking at his Camp Tsha-Tshi official residence after talks with Likulia, who has named a 28-member government with a general close to Mobutu in the key post of interior minister and responsible for national reconciliation.
